mktApiDocs.title: API documentation
mktApiDocs.subtitle: Connect Whasalia with n8n, Make, Zapier, your ERP or your own code: read and create contacts, send messages, manage orders and bookings, and get every event as it happens with webhooks.

intro.body: It's a JSON REST API. Every route hangs from this address and only answers over HTTPS:
intro.json: Send `Content-Type: application/json` on POST and PATCH. Responses carry the resource in `data`.
intro.ids: Ids are UUIDs. Phones use international format (`+51987654321`).
intro.dates: Date-times are ISO 8601 in UTC. Booking dates and times use the business's time zone.
intro.scope: Each key belongs to one business and only sees and changes that business's data.

auth.body: Create a key in **Settings → Integrations → API keys** (admins only) and send it in the `Authorization` header of every request. `GET /me` tests the connection:
auth.safety: The key is shown only once. Keep it as a secret on your server (never in a public web page or app). If it leaks, revoke it on the same screen and create another: it stops working instantly.

scopes.body: When you create the key you choose what it can do. `read` reads everything, `write` reads and writes everything; the others grant read and write on a single resource. Use only the ones the integration needs.

errors.body: Errors answer with the HTTP status and always the same shape. `details` (when present) points to the field or carries useful data, like alternative times.

pagination.body: Lists return up to `limit` items (25 by default, 100 max), newest first, and a `next_cursor`. For the next page repeat the request with `cursor=<next_cursor>`; when it's `null` there are no more.

limits.body: Each key can make 120 requests per minute. Every response carries `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset`; above it you get 429 with `Retry-After` in seconds. Attempts with invalid keys are also limited per IP.

webhooks.body: Set them up in **Settings → Integrations → Webhooks**: choose the URL (public https) and the events. Each event arrives as a POST like this:
webhooks.verifyBody: Each endpoint has a secret (`whsec_…`) shown when you create or rotate it. The `X-Whasalia-Signature` header carries `t` (Unix seconds) and `v1` = HMAC-SHA256 of the text `<t>.<body>` with that secret. Compute it over the body exactly as received and reject signatures older than 5 minutes. Node.js example:
webhooks.retriesBody: Answer with a 2xx status within 10 seconds (redirects count as failures). On failure we retry after 1 min, 5 min, 30 min, 2 h, 6 h and 24 h, with the same event `id`: use it to avoid processing twice. After 20 failures in a row the endpoint is disabled and admins are notified. The screen shows every delivery with its response and lets you resend it.
webhooks.eventsBody: `data` carries the resources with the same fields as the API (`message`, `contact`, `order`…).
